passages.note: Bill status page shows Mesnard as prime sponsor of SCR1040 but prints no operative text.

passages.provision_quote: For any employee who customarily and regularly receives tips or gratuities from patrons or others, the employer may pay a wage up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage established by statute if the employer can establish by the employer's records of charged tips or gratuities or by the employee’s declaration for federal insurance contributions act purposes that for each week, when adding tips or gratuities received to wages paid, the employee received not less than the minimum wage plus $2 for all hours worked.
passages.note: The operative section creates a tipped-worker carve-out below the statutory minimum wage; the former short title appears only inside a [deleted: …] fence and is not quoted.
Senate Final Reading #2 roll call recording Mesnard's Aye; 12 of 30 members voted No, so it is not near-unanimous.

rows.reasoning: Mesnard prime-sponsored and voted Aye on SCR1040 (2024), which would let an employer of a tipped worker "pay a wage up to twenty-five percent per hour less than the minimum wage established by statute" subject to a tips-plus-$2 floor. That is a carve-out for one category of worker: it neither "Hold[s] the wage floor at its current level and let[s] the market set pay above it" nor does it "Remove the wage floor entirely and let employers and workers set pay by agreement" — the statutory floor and a $2 premium still bind. The measure therefore shows a side (against the floor's full application) but matches no rung's clauses, and ruling out the raise-the-floor rungs is not evidence for either remaining rung.
